mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows and increases equity valuations.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand that reduces corporate revenue expectations and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative returns: 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), reduced wage pressures lower corporate labor costs and boost profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of consumer spending (RSAFS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as it signals robust economic activity and stronger corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in high RSAFS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100 (INDPRO < 100), it signals a manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output capacity and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% (FEDFUNDS < 4.5) combined with a CPI index above 315 (CPIAUCSL > 315) signals a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically precedes market corrections due to rising real rates and reduced profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS < 4.5 and CPIAUCSL > 315 fails to predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During strong manufacturing output regimes (INDPRO > 102), eased supply chain constraints expand corporate production capacity and boost revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO > 102.
